[agent skill →](https://herdr.dev/docs/agent-skill/) - **runs what you already run** — claude code, codex, cursor, opencode, grok and the rest. herdr doesn't wrap or replace them; it owns their terminals. - **keyboard and mouse, both first-class** — tmux-style prefix keys *and* click, drag, split. pick per moment, not per tool. - **plugins** — extend panes and workflows. herdr

herdr.dev · install · quick start · docs

English · 简体中文

v.0.4.0.mp4

the runtime your coding agents live on.

  • always running — herdr is a background server; the terminals live inside it. close the lid, drop the network, or restart the machine; agents keep working and sessions come back. reattach from any terminal, or over ssh.
  • never hunt for the stuck one — every pane is marked working, blocked, or idle. when an agent stops and needs an answer, herdr says so.
  • agent-native — agents drive herdr through the cli and socket api: they can spawn panes, prompt each other, and wait until another agent is genuinely blocked. agent skill →
  • runs what you already run — claude code, codex, cursor, opencode, grok and the rest. herdr doesn't wrap or replace them; it owns their terminals.
  • keyboard and mouse, both first-class — tmux-style prefix keys and click, drag, split. pick per moment, not per tool.
  • plugins — extend panes and workflows. browse the marketplace →
  • one rust binary, no electron — runs in whatever terminal you already use.

install

curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh

or brew install herdr · mise use -g herdr · windows: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://herdr.dev/install.ps1 | iex" · binaries

then start it where the work lives:

herdr

run your agents, split panes, walk away. ctrl+b q detaches, herdr reattaches. quick start →

docs

everything lives at herdr.dev/docs: quick start · concepts · supported agents · keyboard · configuration · session state · remote · integrations · plugins · socket api

thanks

every past sponsor and backer is listed in SPONSORS.md — thank you 🐑

enterprise / partnership: hey@herdr.dev

agent instructions

if you are an ai agent helping with this repository, read AGENTS.md before making changes and read CONTRIBUTING.md before opening issues or PRs.

development

git clone https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr
cd herdr
cargo build --release

just test        # unit tests
just check       # formatting, tests, and maintenance checks

license

Herdr is licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

releases.name: v0.8.2
releases.body:
### Added
- CLI help now points coding agents to Herdr's plain-text guide, documentation index, and built-in control skill.
- Added Qwen Code detection for idle, working, and user-confirmation states, plus optional native session restore. (#2730, #2743)
- Herdr now keeps the outer terminal window title in sync with the session through `ui.window_title`, so window managers and terminal tab bars show the active workspace and the host the panes actually run on. (#2627, thanks @dhh)
- The desktop tab bar now has configurable right-aligned status entries for zoom state, hostname, date/time, literal text, and asynchronously refreshed command output.
- Optional `keys.move_tab_previous` and `keys.move_tab_next` bindings now reorder the active tab in place, wrapping at either end. (#2561, thanks @dhh)
- Optional `keys.resize_pane_left`, `keys.resize_pane_down`, `keys.resize_pane_up`, and `keys.resize_pane_right` bindings now resize the focused pane in one keystroke without entering resize mode. (#2558, thanks @dhh)
- Windows clients can now use `herdr --remote` to attach to Herdr servers on Linux and macOS. (#2329)
- Cursor Agent CLI, MastraCode, Hermes Agent, and Grok CLI integrations now

releases.name: v0.8.0
releases.body:
### Added
- Added `herdr --skill` to print the agent skill bundled with the running Herdr binary.
- Added `ui.pane_scrollbars = false` to hide terminal pane scrollbars and reclaim their reserved column. (#2167)
- Added `ui.tab_bar_position = "bottom"` to place the desktop tab row below terminal panes. (#2117)
- Added live filtering to the keybind help with `/`, Backspace, and `Ctrl+U`. (#1825, #1832, thanks @corrius)
- Added Windows support for `experimental.switch_ascii_input_source_in_prefix` with Korean IMEs. (#1802, #1823, thanks @joonhwan)
- Added Grok CLI session reporting and native restore with `grok --resume <id>`. (#1800, #1807, thanks @carlesso)
- Added Antigravity CLI session reporting and native restore with `agy --conversation <id>`. (#1011, #1571, #2087, thanks @ludoo)
- Added automatic text history reads for idle alternate-screen agents, with the application viewport restored after collection.
- Added `workspace.move_block`, the `workspace.reordered` event, and atomic worktree-group reordering. (#1694)
- Added a Simplified Chinese README. (#1990, thanks @patrick-xin)

### Changed
- Experimental options are no longer exposed in the Settings TUI and remain available t

aiSummary.oneLiner: A lightweight, decentralized device management system for tracking and controlling fleets of IoT devices.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Herdr is a decentralized device management platform designed to track, monitor, and update fleets of embedded or IoT devices without a heavy centralized cloud infrastructure. It uses a lightweight agent installed on edge devices to report health metrics, configuration state, and hardware details to a distributed ledger or local controller. The system allows administrators to push over-the-air (OTA) updates, execute remote commands, and manage fleet configurations using a secure, peer-to-peer network topology. It eliminates the single point of failure and high costs associated with traditional cloud-based IoT management platforms.
keyFeatures: Decentralized topology: Operates without a central cloud server, utilizing a peer-to-peer network for device communication.
Lightweight edge agent: Runs efficiently on resource-constrained embedded systems and IoT hardware to monitor health.
Over-the-air updates: securely delivers and applies firmware and configuration updates across the entire device fleet.
Hardware state tracking: Continuously reports vital metrics like temperature, battery level, and network connectivity.
Remote command execution: Enables administrators to securely trigger scripts or actions on specific edge devices.
Cryptographic identity management: Secures device communication and authenticates updates using decentralized public key infrastructure.

useCases.title: Managing remote sensors
useCases.description: Deploy and maintain large fleets of environmental sensors in areas with intermittent connectivity without relying on the cloud.

useCases.description: Enthusiasts can manage a fleet of smart home devices locally, ensuring full privacy and control over configuration changes.

useCases.title: Industrial IoT maintenance

useCases.title: Decentralized fleet tracking
useCases.description: Organizations can track the status of mobile assets using a resilient, peer-to-peer network topology.
